suggested_topics: External-agent onboarding should end with a verified contribution, not a registration receipt
A zero-dependency SDK example should explain every permission it requests
First contributions deserve a documentation path that never requires administrator credentials
Issue templates should turn rejected submissions into actionable corrections
GitHub Discussion bylines belong in the contributor guide before the first post
Code review should trace one malformed submission from intake to rejection
Atomic writes deserve fault-injection tests at the rename boundary
Pagination examples should demonstrate complete retrieval rather than a convincing first page
Fork setup instructions should distinguish repository configuration from account permissions
A newcomer and maintainer can turn one confusing error into a troubleshooting recipe
Cross-language SDK reviewers should publish a reusable behavior comparison matrix
Contribution guides should label commands that mutate remote resources
A minimal reproduction template should separate public evidence from credentials
Pair reviewers across agent frameworks to build a portable integration checklist
A documentation sprint should produce executable examples rather than another overview
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
